properties.title: Causal Transformer for Estimating Counterfactual Outcomes

membership.reason: Causal Transformer models multi-step-ahead counterfactual clinical outcome trajectories under time-varying treatments using cross-attentional balancing.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L3 counterfactual longitudinal outcome world model (WT_EHR, BP_COMPARE).

properties.backbone: 3-subnetwork Causal Transformer with cross-attentions and Counterfactual Domain Confusion (CDC) loss

properties.flow: Covariates X_t + treatments A_t + outcomes Y_t + static V -> balanced representation Phi_t -> multi-step counterfactual outcomes

properties.purpose: One- and multi-step-ahead counterfactual outcome estimation from observational longitudinal data.
properties.environment: Synthetic tumor-growth + semi-synthetic MIMIC-III ICU data

assertions.rationale: Three parallel Transformer subnetworks for covariates, treatments, and outcomes with cross-attention.
Balanced latent representation Phi_t across time.
Captures long-range dependencies in patient history H_t.
Time-varying treatment sequence A_t and future intervention sequence a_{t+1:t+tau}.

Evaluated matched alternative-action counterfactual predictions from the same patient history on synthetic tumor growth (all 4 treatment combinations at tau=1; 10 single-sliding and 10 random alternative trajectories at tau=1..6, Fig. 2 & Tables 9-11) and semi-synthetic MIMIC-III (all 2^3=8 treatment combinations at tau=1; 10 random alternative trajectories at tau=1..10, Table 1). Real-world MIMIC-III evaluation (Table 2) is factual-only due to unobserved counterfactuals.
One- and multi-step-ahead counterfactual trajectory prediction.
Causal Transformer trained end-to-end with CDC adversarial balancing loss.

Multi-step outcome predictions conditioned on specified future static treatment plans; quantitatively evaluated on synthetic tumor growth (Fig. 2, Tables 9-11), semi-synthetic MIMIC-III (Table 1), and real-world MIMIC-III factual outcomes (Table 2).

Evaluated one-step (tau=1) and autoregressive multi-step (tau=2..6, 2..10, 2..5) outcome prediction across synthetic tumor growth (Fig. 2, Tables 9-11), semi-synthetic MIMIC-III (Table 1), and real-world MIMIC-III (Table 2).
Outperforms RMSN, CRN, and G-Net on synthetic and semi-synthetic MIMIC-III counterfactual benchmarks.

evidence_fragments.content: we combine three transformer subnetworks with separate inputs for time-varying covariates, previous treatments, and previous outcomes into a joint network with in-between cross-attentions.

[paraphrase (visual p.2)] Figure 1 shows the Causal Transformer overview with three parallel Transformer subnetworks for treatments A_t/a_t, outcomes Y_t/Y_hat_t, and time-varying covariates X_t plus static covariates V fused through B multi-input blocks with masked self-attention and masked cross-attention, averaged into balanced representation Phi_t feeding outcome network G_Y and treatment classifier G_A for CDC loss over patient history and projection horizon.
During evaluation of multiple-step-ahead prediction, we switch off teacher forcing and autoregressively feed model predictions.
Because we no longer have access to the true counterfactuals, we now report the performance of predicting factual outcomes; see Table 2.

locator.section_or_table: Appendix J.1 Summary of Tumor Growth Simulator

evidence_fragments.content: For each patient in the test set and each time step, we simulate several counterfactual trajectories, depending on τ. For onestep-ahead prediction, we simulate all four combinations of one-step-ahead counterfactual outcomesYt+1. This corresponds to the tumor volume under all possible combinations of treatment assignments.
we then simulate all 23 = 8 counterfactual outcomes. For multiple-step-ahead prediction with τmax = 10, we sample 10 random trajectories for each patient/time step.

capability_assessments.rationale: Three-subnetwork Causal Transformer with CDC adversarial balancing loss implementing persistent latent state Phi_t and autoregressive temporal outcome prediction; evaluated on matched alternative-action counterfactual trajectories from the same patient history in synthetic tumor growth (4 one-step / 10 multi-step trajectories) and semi-synthetic MIMIC-III (8 one-step / 10 multi-step trajectories), while real-world MIMIC-III evaluates factual outcomes only (L3).

limitations: Evaluated on synthetic and semi-synthetic MIMIC-III benchmarks; focuses on static future treatment sequences rather than closed-loop dynamic policies.

Real-world MIMIC-III evaluation (Table 2, Section 5.3) assesses factual outcome prediction only because ground-truth counterfactuals are unobserved; future time-varying covariates are masked rather than rolled out during multi-step prediction.
notes: All 37 physical PDF pages extracted/read; page 2 visually inspected via rendered PNG.

legacy_cells.B: Causal Transformer for Estimating Counterfactual Outcomes
legacy_cells.O: Critically ill ICU patient trajectories; synthetic lung-cancer tumor growth
legacy_cells.S: How are future patient outcomes estimated under specified treatment interventions, including ICU diastolic blood pressure under vasopressors and mechanical ventilation?
legacy_cells.T: 5,000 patients randomly selected from ICU stays of at least 30 hours; stays truncated at 60 hours
legacy_cells.V: Inform treatment-plan choice using individualized predicted outcomes (author-stated; decision utility not evaluated)
legacy_cells.AI: Time-varying covariates (25 ICU vital signs); past treatments (vasopressors; mechanical ventilation); past outcome (diastolic blood pressure); static covariates (gender; ethnicity; age)
legacy_cells.AJ: Three transformer subnetworks with masked multi-head self-attention and cross-attention; linear input projections, feed-forward layers, layer normalization, and residual connections
legacy_cells.AM: Cross-attention exchanges information among treatment, outcome, and covariate subnetworks; their representations are averaged into a shared balanced representation
legacy_cells.AN: Forward- and backward-fill imputation for missing values in MIMIC-extract preprocessing
legacy_cells.AZ: t-SNE visualizations of learned balanced representations by treatment and next outcome; treatment balancing was challenging in severe cases with few untreated patients
legacy_cells.BD: Two binary treatment inputs in real-world experiments: vasopressors and mechanical ventilation; no dose or timing attributes specified
legacy_cells.BL: Hourly aggregation for MIMIC-extract; tumor-growth simulator advances in daily steps
legacy_cells.BN: Counterfactual domain confusion (CDC) adversarial loss to learn outcome-predictive representations that are non-predictive of current treatment assignment
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted future patient outcomes, including counterfactual outcome sequences under specified treatment interventions
legacy_cells.BT: Outcome prediction network GY; auxiliary current-treatment classifier GA for CDC training
legacy_cells.BV: Factual next-outcome mean squared error plus CDC adversarial domain-confusion and current-treatment classification cross-entropy losses
legacy_cells.CD: Up to 10 prediction steps in synthetic/semi-synthetic experiments; up to 5 steps in real MIMIC-III experiments
legacy_cells.CV: Consistency; sequential ignorability (no unobserved confounding conditional on observed history); sequential overlap
legacy_cells.CX: Counterfactual predictions evaluated against known ground-truth counterfactuals in fully synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments; real MIMIC-III evaluation used factual outcomes
legacy_cells.DN: MIMIC-III (via MIMIC-extract); tumor-growth simulator; semi-synthetic MIMIC-III-derived benchmark
legacy_cells.DQ: Real MIMIC-III: 5,000 ICU patients; semi-synthetic: 1,000 patients; tumor-growth simulator: 10,000 training, 1,000 validation, and 1,000 test trajectories per confounding level
legacy_cells.DX: Real MIMIC-III factual one-step outcome prediction: RMSE 4.59 ± 0.09 (diastolic blood pressure)
legacy_cells.DY: Real MIMIC-III factual multi-step RMSE: τ=2 8.99 ± 0.21; τ=3 9.59 ± 0.22; τ=4 9.91 ± 0.26; τ=5 10.14 ± 0.29
legacy_cells.EB: Yes—counterfactual predictions were evaluated under alternative treatment assignments/sequences against known simulated outcomes
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations varied positional encoding, attentional dropout, cross-attention, EMA, balancing loss, gradient reversal, and a single-subnetwork encoder-decoder variant
legacy_cells.EL: Treatment balancing became challenging for severe tumor cases because few such patients received no treatment
legacy_cells.FL: Three parallel masked transformer subnetworks encode past treatments, outcomes, and time-varying covariates, with static covariates supplied to all; cross-attention and pooling produce a balanced latent representation; autoregressive outcome prediction and an auxiliary treatment classifier are trained with a CDC loss; no planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FM: The authors propose the Causal Transformer: three interacting transformer subnetworks for long-range trajectory dependencies, trained end-to-end with a counterfactual domain confusion loss.
legacy_cells.FN: On real MIMIC-III factual prediction, CT achieved RMSE 4.59 ± 0.09 at one step and 10.14 ± 0.29 at five steps, outperforming the reported baselines; counterfactual ground-truth evaluation was limited to synthetic/semi-synthetic data.
legacy_cells.FO: For real-world MIMIC-III data, true counterfactual outcomes were unavailable, so the authors evaluated factual outcome prediction instead.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify simple LSTM-based methods as limited in capturing complex, long-range dependencies among time-varying confounders.
legacy_cells.FR: The paper does not demonstrate clinical benefit, prospective validation, real-world counterfactual accuracy, treatment recommendation quality, planning/control, or deployment; real MIMIC-III results are factual-prediction metrics, while counterfactual validation uses simulated data.
